import FormalConjecturesUtil
/-!

# Erdős Problem 354
*Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/354](https://www.erdosproblems.com/354)

-/
namespace Erdos354

/-- The sequence `⌊a⌋, ⌊γ * a⌋, ⌊γ ^ 2 * a⌋, ..., ⌊γ ^ i * a⌋, ...`. -/
noncomputable def FloorMultiples (a γ : ℝ) (n : ℕ) : ℤ := ⌊γ ^ n * a⌋

/-- The sequence `⌊a⌋, ⌊b⌋, ⌊γ * a⌋, ⌊γ * b⌋, ... ⌊γ ^ i * a⌋, ⌊γ ^ i * b⌋, ...` -/
noncomputable def FloorMultiples.interleave (a b γ : ℝ) (n : ℕ) : ℤ :=
  if n % 2 = 0 then
    FloorMultiples a γ (n / 2)
  else
    FloorMultiples b γ (n / 2)

/-- Let $\alpha,\beta\in \mathbb{R}_{>0}$ such that $\alpha/\beta$ is irrational. Is the multiset
$$\{ \lfloor \alpha\rfloor,\lfloor 2\alpha\rfloor,\lfloor 4\alpha\rfloor,\ldots\}\cup
\{ \lfloor \beta\rfloor,\lfloor 2\beta\rfloor,\lfloor 4\beta\rfloor,\ldots\}$$ complete? -/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_354.parts.i : answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ᵉ (α > 0) (β > 0), Irrational (α / β) →
    IsAddCompleteNatSeq' (FloorMultiples.interleave α β 2) := by
  sorry

/-- Let $\alpha,\beta\in \mathbb{R}_{>0}$ such that $\alpha/\beta$ is irrational. Is
$$\{ \lfloor \alpha\rfloor,\lfloor \gamma\alpha\rfloor,\lfloor \gamma^2\alpha\rfloor,\ldots\}\cup
\{ \lfloor \beta\rfloor,\lfloor \gamma\beta\rfloor,\lfloor \gamma^2\beta\rfloor,\ldots\}$$ complete? -/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_354.parts.ii : answer(sorry) ↔ ∃ γ ∈ Set.Ioo (1 : ℝ) 2, ∀ᵉ (α > 0) (β > 0), Irrational (α / β) →
    IsAddCompleteNatSeq' (FloorMultiples.interleave α β γ) := by
  sorry

end Erdos354

status_issues.source_status: The second question has an affirmative answer as a consequence of Hegyvári's published 1989 Theorem 4. It states that A_{a,b,c} is complete whenever a is a non-dyadic positive real. For γ = √2, the sequence in part (ii) splits into four base-2 sequences with parameters α, β, √2 α, and √2 β. Irrationality of α/β ensures that at least one of α,β is non-dyadic. Three of these four sequences therefore satisfy Theorem 4, and adding the fourth preserves completeness. The main problem page's global OPEN label remains appropriate for part (i), not for this consequence.
status_issues.evidence: Hegyvári (1989), §4, Theorem 4, p. 151: “If α is i.d.f. then A_{αβγ} is complete”; i.d.f. is defined on p. 149 as a non-terminating binary expansion. Full paper: https://real-j.mtak.hu/7450/1/ActaMathHung_53.pdf. Hegyvári also explicitly recalls this result on p. 7 of his 1991 paper. The four-stream identities for γ = √2 were independently checked in Lean.
status_issues.suggested_change: Change only part (ii) to category research solved and replace answer(sorry) by answer(True). Cite Hegyvári (1989), Theorem 4, and explain the γ = √2 deduction.

reformulations.difference: The source uses two finite exponent sets and sufficiently large natural-number targets. Lean instead uses finite subsets of one interleaved index sequence, with eventual completeness over ℤ.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Index 2n supplies ⌊2^n α⌋ and index 2n+1 supplies ⌊2^n β⌋. Splitting any finite index set by parity yields exactly the source's two finite exponent sets; conversely, their even and odd images form the required finite index set. This preserves multiplicities, including coincident values. Eventual truth over ℤ is equivalent to truth for all natural numbers beyond a natural threshold. Both the representability equivalence and the full quantified equivalence were proved in /workspace/review/equivalence.lean.

reformulations.difference: The same interleaved, integer-valued completeness formulation is used for the source's question about replacing 2 by some γ ∈ (1,2).
reformulations.equivalence_argument: The parity-splitting and integer/natural threshold equivalences hold for every real γ, without additional assumptions. Applying them beneath the existential γ and universal α,β quantifiers gives the explicit two-sum formulation. Set.Ioo 1 2 is exactly 1 < γ ∧ γ < 2. The full quantified equivalence was proved in /workspace/review/equivalence.lean.
